case_name: Juhi Chugh vs M/S Govind Textile Pvt. Ltd. And Others

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Juhi Chugh, wife and sole proprietor of business
parties.respondent_defendant: M/s Govind Textile Pvt. Ltd. and others

facts_of_case: Petitioner's husband was signatory of cheque; petitioner claims she had no role in business, which is a sole proprietorship.

legal_principles.principle: Before any person can be summoned to face a criminal trial, it is the duty of the magistrate who searches for the prime evidence which attributes some role that makes out a penal offence.
legal_principles.held: The order of something can only be mechanical and with considering the role.

legal_principles.principle: The director's liability must be determined when the offence was committed and merely being a party to the resolution would not be sufficient.
legal_principles.held: Similarly, in S and S Pharmaceuticals versus Mothanwala 2007 RCR criminal 126, Supreme Court held that the director's liability must be determined when the offence was committed and merely being a party to the resolution would not be sufficient.
cited_cases: S and S Pharmaceuticals versus Mothanwala, (2007) RCR criminal 126

outcome.final_order: The petition under section 482 Cr.P.C. is allowed and the complaint is quashed.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for quashing of complaint
responding to summons in cheque bounce case
defending against allegations of cheque issuance
